# Onboarding Addendum Implementation Plan

> **Executed and superseded (3 Oct 2026).** After execution the main BRD became v4.4 and the addendum's base switched from v4.3 to v4.4: parts 01 to 04 now say "BRD v4.4" where this plan's content blocks say "BRD v4.3", and `build.py` carries the v4.4 names. The parts in `parts/` are authoritative; this plan is kept as the record of how they were written. Task 15 was not run: the combined review pack is `review/metis-review-pack-round3.zip` with `review/gpt-review-prompt-round3.md`.

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Produce the supplementary BRD "BRD Addendum: Onboarding in 30 minutes" (Markdown and Word editions), 12 new wireframes (46 to 57), the tool changes that check them together with BRD v4.3, and a review pack for the external GPT review.

**Architecture:** The addendum is written as pandoc Markdown parts in `brd/source/addendum-onboarding/parts/` and built by the existing `brd/source/build.py`, run with the document name as an argument. The main build ignores every screen that cites an `ONB-` requirement, so the BRD v4.3 outputs stay identical; the addendum build checks those screens against the identifiers of v4.3 and of the addendum together. Wireframes follow the existing HTML conventions and tools (`wireframes/tools/check.py`, `render.mjs`, `build-index.mjs`).

**Tech Stack:** Python 3 (stdlib), pandoc 3.9, LibreOffice `soffice`, poppler `pdftotext`, macOS `sips`, Node 24 with `puppeteer-core` and the local Google Chrome, plain HTML and CSS with `brand/tokens.css`.

**Spec:** `brd/source/addendum-onboarding/2026-10-02-onboarding-design.md` (approved 2 Oct 2026). Also read: `brd/source/addendum-onboarding/option-catalogue.md` and the three notes in `brd/source/addendum-onboarding/research/` (sources of every market claim).

## Global Constraints

- No em dash (U+2014) and no en dash (U+2013) in any file this plan creates or changes. Use a comma, a colon or the word "to".
- Never edit generated files by hand: `brd/*.md`, `brd/*.docx`, `wireframes/manifest.json`, `wireframes/index.html`, `wireframes/wireframes-digest.md`, `wireframes/png/*.png`. Regenerate them with the tools.
- Do not change `brd/source/parts/*.md` (the content of BRD v4.3).
- The BRD v4.3 Markdown edition `brd/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.3.md` must be byte-identical before and after this plan (sha256 recorded in Task 1, compared in Task 14).
- Writing `\u2013` or `\u2014` into a file with an editing tool can turn the escape into the character itself; after editing `build.py`, run `python3 -c "import sys;t=open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8').read();print(chr(0x2013) in t, chr(0x2014) in t)" brd/source/build.py` and expect `False False`.
- No git commands: the folder is not a git repository and the developer forbids automatic commits. Where a TDD cycle would commit, record the result in the task's checklist instead.
- The addendum is written in English, like BRD v4.3; the GPT review prompt is written in Vietnamese, like `review/gpt-review-prompt-round2.md`.
- Identifier formats (they must match the regexes in `brd/source/build.py`): requirements `ONB-01` to `ONB-40`; rules `BR-43` to `BR-50`; decisions `D-32` to `D-39`; questions `Q-14` to `Q-18`; assumptions `A-08` to `A-10`; module `M23`; sources `S7` to `S13`. A defining row starts the line: `| ONB-01 | ...`.
- Requirement tables have exactly five columns in this order: `| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Pri | Source |`. The build reads the priority from the second-to-last cell (`P0` or `P1`) and the source from the last cell.
- Every market claim carries `[Source: <URL or S-code>, <date>]` or `[Unverified - confirm before applying]`; never invent a number, a URL or a product capability.
- Executive-facing questions contain no preset amount or percentage (spec 2.4). A boundary appears only as a consequence computed from the client's data.
- Wireframe sample data for the onboarding screens comes only from "Reference A: Nova Energy sample data" below; numbers must match across screens.

## Review Focus

These five failure modes are the most likely to hurt the people who will use the output (the product owner and the GPT reviewer); each has a check in the task that owns it.

1. **A screen cites a requirement but does not show it** (the GPT round-2 review flagged "weak coverage"). Expected: every ID in a screen's `wf:requirements` is named in at least one of that screen's annotations. Check: the annotation-coverage snippet in each wireframe task (Tasks 8 to 13) and again for all twelve screens in Task 14.
2. **The addendum states a value that differs from the approved spec** (cap of 10 cards, 14-day undo window, 7-day onboarding token, 90-day retention of security-event content, three framing questions, 27 P0 and 13 P1 requirements). Expected: each value appears in the addendum exactly as in the spec. Check: the value grep in Task 14.
3. **Sample data disagrees between screens** (34 projects, EUR 214.6M, 14 projects routed to the executive, 31 delegated items, 6 cards answered). Expected: the same figures everywhere. Check: the sample-data grep in Task 14.
4. **An amendment misstates BRD v4.3** (for example the current priority of CHG-10 or the wording of the out-of-scope line). Expected: every "current" value quoted in the amendments table matches the v4.3 Markdown edition. Check: the amendment cross-check in Task 14.
5. **The review pack is incomplete or points to missing files.** Expected: every file the prompt names is inside the zip. Check: the zip listing check in Task 15.

## Reference B: wireframe screen skeleton and shared onboarding components

Every new screen is one file in `wireframes/screens/` built on this skeleton (compare `wireframes/screens/36-workspace-setup.html`):

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>SCREEN TITLE · Metis wireframe</title>
<meta name="wf:id" content="SCREEN-ID">
<meta name="wf:title" content="SCREEN TITLE">
<meta name="wf:area" content="AREA">
<meta name="wf:phase" content="MVP">
<meta name="wf:requirements" content="SPACE SEPARATED IDS">
<meta name="wf:poc" content="">
<meta name="wf:summary" content="ONE SENTENCE">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../brand/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/wireframe.css">
</head>
<body data-shell="SHELL" data-tenant="Nova Energy" data-user="RO">
<main>
  <!-- sections; each section that shows a requirement carries data-req="IDS" -->
</main>
<section class="wf-notes">
  <h2>Annotations</h2>
  <ol>
    <li><span class="anno" data-n="1"></span><span><span class="req">ONB-01, ONB-02</span> Annotation text.</span></li>
  </ol>
</section>
<script src="../assets/shell.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

Rules for every screen:
- An annotation marker `<span class="anno" data-n="N"></span>` on the screen for each note N, and a note for each marker (`check.py` enforces both).
- Every ID listed in `wf:requirements` appears in the `.req` span of at least one note.
- Future capabilities use `<span class="tag future">Planned V2</span>`, never a disabled look; AI actions use the square avatar `<span class="av ai">AI</span>`; people use round avatars `<span class="av">RO</span>`.
- Status always shows a shape and a word, never colour alone (use `.chip`, `.rag`, `.fresh` and the onboarding badges below).
- The screen's main title is an `<h1 class="title">` (one per screen), so assistive technology has a heading to jump to; symbol-only icon glyphs carry `aria-hidden="true"` (ruling made during execution, from the review of screens 46 and 47).
- Encode `&` as `&amp;` in HTML text (for example `Retail &amp; Digital`).
- On every screen with an `ob-head`, the step state is also written in text: the current step carries `aria-current="step"`, and the clock reads "Step N of 4 · Your time so far: X" (for example "Step 3 of 4 · Your time so far: 14 min"), with N the position of the step marked `cur` (ruling made during execution: the CSS-only state was invisible to screen readers and to the text digest).
- In the screen specs of Tasks 8 to 13, an annotation written as "`ONB-02, ONB-27` Text" becomes `<li><span class="anno" data-n="N"></span><span><span class="req">ONB-02, ONB-27</span> Text</span></li>`, numbered in the order listed, and "marker N" means `<span class="anno" data-n="N"></span>` placed at that spot on the screen.

Shared onboarding components (added to `wireframes/assets/wireframe.css` by Task 2; use them instead of inline copies):

```python
# Builds a BRD document (.docx and .md) from its parts, with generated traceability and wireframe references.
# Usage: python3 build.py [main|addendum-onboarding]   (default main; needs pandoc, LibreOffice soffice, poppler pdftotext, macOS sips)
# main: parts/*.md, legacy/brd_v2_v3_converted.md, ../../vistax-poc-screens/, ../../wireframes/manifest.json -> BRD v4.3
# addendum-onboarding: addendum-onboarding/parts/*.md and the screens that cite ONB- requirements -> the onboarding addendum;
#   identifiers of BRD v4.3 count as known references, and the main build ignores the addendum's screens.
# Outputs: ../<NAME>.docx, ../<NAME>.md, ../images/poc-NN.jpg (main only)
import html, re, shutil, struct, subprocess, sys, tempfile
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BRD = HERE.parent
ROOT = BRD.parent
DOC = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "main"
MAIN = DOC == "main"
ADDENDA = {  # name -> (output name, footer text, sentence that opens the body after the table of contents)
    "addendum-onboarding": ("Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_Addendum_Onboarding_v1.0",
                            "Metis · Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence &amp; Governance Platform  |  BRD Addendum: Onboarding v1.0",
                            "This addendum supplements BRD v4.3 without editing it"),
}
if not MAIN and DOC not in ADDENDA:
    sys.exit(f"unknown document: {DOC}; use main or one of {sorted(ADDENDA)}")
NAME, FOOTER, ANCHOR = (("Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.3", None, "The two supplied BRD files are")
                        if MAIN else ADDENDA[DOC])
OUT_DOCX, OUT_MD = BRD / f"{NAME}.docx", BRD / f"{NAME}.md"
POC_DIR = ROOT / "vistax-poc-screens"
WF_DIR = ROOT / "wireframes"
MAIN_PARTS = sorted((HERE / "parts").glob("*.md"))
PARTS = MAIN_PARTS if MAIN else sorted((HERE / DOC / "parts").glob("*.md"))
if not PARTS:
    sys.exit(f"no parts for {DOC}")
FIGURES = ["04-tenant-admin-ai-access", "08-profile-ai-access", "11-lifecycle-framework-designer",
           "12-gate-review", "14-executive-cockpit", "15-workspace-dashboard", "38-my-approvals", "42-editor-states"]

md = "\n".join(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in PARTS)

PREFIXES = "PLT|TEN|WSP|GOV|MCP|CHR|WBS|BLD|PLN|OVW|CHG|RPT|RSK|MVP|EXE|REG|RMP|RES|INV|STR|ANL|AIC|ONB"
ADDENDUM_PREFIXES = {"ONB"}  # requirement prefixes defined by an addendum, never by BRD v4.3
ROW_ID = re.compile(r"^\|\s*((?:%s|BR|D|Q|A|C)-\d{2})\s*\|" % PREFIXES)
REQ_ID = re.compile(r"^(?:%s|BR)-\d{2}$" % PREFIXES)
cells = lambda line: [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
problems = []

# ---- defined IDs and their Source cells
def table_ids(text):
    found = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = ROW_ID.match(line)
        if m:
            if m.group(1) in found:
                problems.append(f"duplicate ID {m.group(1)}")
            found[m.group(1)] = cells(line)
    return found
defined = table_ids(md)
sources = {rid: c[-1] for rid, c in defined.items() if REQ_ID.match(rid)}
main_ids = set(defined) if MAIN else set(table_ids("\n".join(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in MAIN_PARTS)))
known = set(defined) | main_ids  # identifiers that text and screens may cite
if not MAIN:
    problems += [f"{rid} is already defined in BRD v4.3" for rid in defined if rid in main_ids]
```

````markdown
# 7. Functional Requirements: Module M23

## M23 Onboarding & Data Intake (ONB)

Purpose: take a new client from nothing to a working workspace in 30 minutes of the main setup person's effort (Section 4.1). Metis reads whatever the client already has, builds the company as a draft in a Draft workspace, asks only what it cannot read, launches with one approval and hands the rest to the right owners. Requirements marked P0 belong to Release 1, as in BRD v4.3; P1 follows.

Wireframes: {{WF:ONB}}.

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Pri | Source |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|------|--------------|
| ONB-01 | **Onboarding session.** Each new tenant starts with one onboarding session for its first workspace, created at provisioning (TEN-01) or by a tenant admin. The session holds the pre-filled facts, the framing answers, the inputs and their source fragments, per-field provenance, questions, delegated items, X-ray findings, the provider and model version of the onboarding AI, and the batch ID stamped on every record it creates. It is resumable until launch and stays open after launch for delegated items, suggestions and the undo window. | (1) Signing in again after closing the browser reopens the session at the same step with nothing lost. (2) Every record created by the session carries its batch ID. (3) A session that used the onboarding AI shows the provider and model version it ran on. | P0 | S7; WSP-14 |
| ONB-02 | **Facts pre-filled from the sales discovery.** When creating the tenant, the provider operator records scope, main kind of work, reporting currency and fiscal year and, when the sales discovery gave them, the answers to the three framing questions (ONB-03); the executive confirms them in one tap or changes any of them. The main kind of work sets the starting pack (ONB-27) and the MVP objects on or off (MVP-04). The operator may also pre-select the onboarding AI; it stays off until a tenant admin accepts the consent screen (ONB-22). | (1) A tenant created with pre-filled facts opens the framing screen with those values selected and labelled "pre-filled by the Metis team". (2) Currency and fiscal year are confirmed before any value is imported. (3) A pre-selected onboarding AI sends no customer content to the LLM provider until a tenant admin accepts the consent screen. | P0 | S7; TEN-01; D-27; S8 |
| ONB-03 | **Three framing questions, asked outside-in.** The executive answers, or confirms pre-selected answers to, three questions about their own view and decisions: how they want to look at the portfolio, how involved they want to be in project decisions, and what they want to know first every morning. One sentence may replace all three. No question carries a preset amount or percentage; each offers "let Metis work it out"; each answer previews the resulting home screen. | (1) The framing screen shows exactly three questions, none containing a number, each skippable and each answer with a preview of the resulting home screen, on the same screen as the drop zone. (2) A one-sentence answer sets the same values as the three questions. (3) The answers set the portfolio levels, the approval routing and the home view listed in Section 6.3. | P0 | S7 |
| ONB-04 | **Drop and paste anything.** One drop zone accepts many files, folders and zip archives of the supported types (spreadsheets, CSV, Word, PDF, PowerPoint, MS Project MPP and XML, images, saved emails) and pasted text or tables. Uploads are scanned (PLT-07) and limited per plan (TEN-05). The drop zone lists the files that help most for the executive's answers; the reading feed shows what each file yielded and the time left until the draft is ready. Images are read by the provider's vision service once the onboarding AI is enabled (ONB-22); without it they are listed but not read. | (1) A zip of mixed supported files is accepted in one drop and each file appears in the reading feed. (2) An unsupported or oversized file is listed with its reason and does not stop the others. | P0 | S7; S8; PLT-07 |
| ONB-05 | **Exact parsers before AI.** Structured inputs are read by rule-based parsers: spreadsheet cells with formatting and colours, CSV, MS Project XML and MPP, exports from Project Online, Jira, Asana, Smartsheet and monday.com, Word and PDF text with OCR for scans, PowerPoint text and tables, saved emails (message text and attachments). The LLM handles only ambiguous mappings and unstructured content. | (1) An MS Project or Project Online export becomes WBS items with dates and dependencies without an LLM call. (2) A red, amber or green cell in a tracker becomes the project's declared health. | P0 | S7; S8; S9 |
| ONB-06 | **Onboarding agent.** When the tenant has enabled it (ONB-22), a third-party LLM called through an API (D-32) reads source fragments as quoted data, maps them to Metis records, resolves the same project or person written differently across files, detects contradictions, matches the operating model against the starting packs (ONB-27) and raises questions while reading. The agent is one more client of the MCP server: it writes only through the setup tool group (ONB-07), with a short-lived onboarding token bound to the executive, the tenant and the Draft workspace. Metis builds no model and trains none. | (1) A project named differently in two files becomes one record that lists both sources. (2) The first question or finding appears while files are still being read (Section 15.2). (3) A write by the agent outside its Draft workspace is refused. | P0 | S7; D-32; S10; BR-43 |
| ONB-07 | **MCP setup tool group.** A prepare-only tool group on the tenant's MCP server (Section 7.1) writes proposals into a Draft workspace and its onboarding session; it never writes into an Active workspace and never publishes, activates, invites or grants roles. Each proposal carries source references, a confidence per field and an idempotency key (PLT-06); validation errors are written so that an LLM can correct itself. The group is off by default for external clients and switched on by a tenant admin (MCP-20). | (1) A setup call never changes an Active workspace: after launch a call carrying a source is stored as a suggestion in the session (ONB-18), and a call outside the workspace its token is bound to is refused. (2) Repeating a call with the same idempotency key changes nothing a second time. (3) A proposal without a source reference, or citing a source that is not in the session, is rejected with a message naming the missing field or the unknown source; on the bring-your-own-AI path a source reported in the call (file name, location, quoted passage) is first recorded in the session as reported by your AI (Section 12.4). | P0 | S7; S10; MCP-08; BR-35 |
| ONB-08 | **Provenance and confidence.** Every value created by onboarding keeps its source (file, location, quoted passage), a confidence band (high, medium, low) and a status (read, assumed, default, confirmed, asked, delegated, conflicting). High-confidence values show their source on hover; medium values carry a "check" badge, and a "check" value still unconfirmed at launch counts as assumed; low and conflicting values become questions; assumed and default values keep their badge until confirmed and, after launch, appear in the responsible owner's attention list; the executive's attention queue (EXE-02) shows the assumed values as one item per owner, with the number still to confirm, together with that owner's overdue delegated tasks (ONB-17), until they are confirmed. The numeric cut-offs of the bands are tuned in Discovery. | (1) Opening any figure of the draft cockpit shows the file and passage it came from. (2) Every value created by onboarding shows a source, or an assumed or default label (BR-45). (3) After launch, an assumed value awaiting confirmation appears in the responsible owner's attention list and is counted, together with that owner's overdue delegated tasks (ONB-17), in that owner's item of the executive's attention queue (EXE-02) until someone confirms or changes it. | P0 | S7; S10 |
| ONB-09 | **The Draft workspace is the draft.** Onboarding writes into a workspace in Draft (WSP-05), which only owners and admins can open: option lists, portfolio tree, a lifecycle draft version (GOV-19 to GOV-21), adopted projects (ONB-10) and member records with proposed roles. Invitations and role grants wait for launch. "Start over" deletes every record the session's batch created in the Draft workspace; the audit log and the session's inputs remain. | (1) Before launch, a member of the tenant does not see the workspace in the switcher. (2) Start over removes every record the batch created in the Draft workspace; the audit log and the session's inputs remain. | P0 | S7; WSP-05 |

## 7.1 MCP setup tool catalogue

Indicative names, fixed in the API design like the tool catalogue of BRD v4.3 (M05). Every tool runs as the user who owns the token, within the tenant (MCP-04), and belongs to one action class (MCP-19). Prepare-only here means that nothing becomes live until a person approves the launch in the application (ONB-15), instead of a confirmation link per call (MCP-08); after launch a setup call that carries a source is stored as a suggestion in the session (ONB-18).

| Tool | Purpose | Class (MCP-19) | Writes to |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|--------------|------------|
| `get_setup_context` | Framing answers, starting pack, record schemas, order of work, rules and the session's open questions | Read | Nothing |
| `propose_profile` | Workspace profile and the irreversible settings | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `propose_option_lists` | Categories, types, labels, statuses with their system states, priorities | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `propose_portfolio_tree` | Portfolios and programs from the chosen view | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `propose_people` | Members with titles and proposed roles; placeholders for people not yet invited | Prepare-only | Draft workspace (no invitation) |
| `propose_projects` | Adopted projects with stage, commitment, budget, dates, owner, sponsor and declared status | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `propose_lifecycle` | Lifecycle draft version: stages, approval points, approvers, quorum, rules | Prepare-only | Lifecycle draft version |
| `propose_project_plan` | WBS items and dependencies from a plan | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `propose_capacity` | Capacity and allocations | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `propose_budget` | Budgets and actuals | Prepare-only | Draft workspace |
| `raise_question` | A gap or contradiction with sources, best guess, owner and treatment | Prepare-only | Onboarding session |
| `record_finding` | A Portfolio X-ray finding with sources and suggested owner | Prepare-only | Onboarding session |
| `check_readiness` | Runs the activation rules (WSP-14), the publish check (GOV-21) and the dry run (ONB-14); returns each failure in plain words | Read | Nothing |

| ID | Business rule | Source |
|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| BR-43 | The onboarding agent and MCP clients using the setup tool group write proposals only into a Draft workspace and its onboarding session; after launch they write suggestions that a person accepts. | S7; BR-35 |
````

````markdown
# 1. About This Addendum

This addendum supplements BRD v4.3 without editing it. It specifies how a new client gets from nothing to a working Metis in 30 minutes of the main setup person's effort, and what that changes in BRD v4.3. Its amendments are listed in Section 13; until a later release merges them, BRD v4.3 remains the baseline and this addendum prevails where it states an amendment.

## 1.1 Why an addendum

To use every capability of Metis, a client sets up a tenant, a workspace with its lifecycle and approvals, people and roles, and its existing projects and data. The second external review (S6) estimated 12 to 24 or more steps for tenant onboarding, 18 to 35 for workspace setup and 15 to 28 for each project. The product owner asked that any client be set up in 30 minutes, without slide tours and without a long wizard, and accepted AI that reads whatever the client already has (S7).

## 1.2 Decisions behind this addendum

Taken by the product owner on 2 October 2026 (S7):

- The 30 minutes measure the hands-on effort of the main setup person until the aha moment (Section 4.1).
- Whatever input the client has is read, converted and imported; what is missing is asked through automated questions or delegated to its owner.
- The users are mostly C-level executives with little time; any executive must understand the process at once and must not be pushed to give up.
- Metis builds no model and trains none. It calls a third-party LLM through an API, enabled by the customer; that AI talks to Metis's own MCP server (the Model Context Protocol interface of BRD v4.3, module M05) to create the records and runs the questions (D-32).
- The data belongs to the customer. Security protects the boundary: other tenants, Metis internals, roles and person-only decisions (Section 11).
- A second path gives prompts and guidance so that the client's own LLM sends the data (Section 12).
- Without the AI, rule-based importers remain the fallback for structured files (Section 9.6).
- Of three approaches considered (Appendix C), the design keeps "draft first", opens with a few questions to the executive and delegates the rest (Section 6).

## 1.3 Identifiers

New identifiers continue the numbering of BRD v4.3: module M23 with the requirement prefix ONB, business rules BR-43 to BR-50, decisions D-32 to D-39, open questions Q-14 to Q-18, assumptions A-08 to A-10, sources S7 to S13 and wireframes 46 to 57. Identifiers of BRD v4.3 keep their meaning; the build of this addendum checks every reference against both documents.

# 2. Executive Summary

Enterprise portfolio tools take weeks to months to implement (Section 3). Metis aims at 30 minutes of the main setup person's effort, because its buyers are executives who will not fill in forms.

The design turns setup from filling in into confirming. The Metis team pre-fills what the sales conversations already established. The executive confirms three questions about their own view and decisions, then drops whatever the company already has: trackers, decks, handbooks, plans, org charts. A third-party LLM, enabled by the customer, reads them and builds the company as a draft, through Metis's own MCP server, inside a Draft workspace: portfolios, adopted in-flight projects, people with proposed roles, the approval flow and a Portfolio X-ray of the problems hidden in those documents. The executive sees their own cockpit after about 15 minutes, answers at most 10 one-tap cards, checks a dry run of the approval flow on three real projects and launches with one approval. Everything else goes to the right owners as pre-filled tasks, and launch never waits for them.

Every value keeps its source. Nothing becomes live until a person approves it; launch can be undone for 14 days by default. The customer's data is theirs to use through any admitted MCP client; the boundary around other tenants, Metis internals and person-only decisions is enforced by architecture and proven by three test suites on every release. Clients that keep the Metis AI switched off use their own AI through the same tools, or rule-based importers.

The addendum adds 40 requirements (27 for Release 1), 8 business rules, 8 decisions and 5 open questions, and amends BRD v4.3 in 20 places (Section 13).

# 3. Where Onboarding Time Goes

| Layer | Who | What must exist | Steps estimated by the second review (S6) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tenant | Tenant admin | Sign-in (SSO or password with MFA), verified domains, users, roles per workspace and project, AI access policy | 12 to 24 or more |
| Workspace | Workspace owner | Profile, option lists, team and roles, lifecycle with approvals, process frameworks, portfolio tree | 18 to 35 |
| Project | Project manager | Project record, charter, business case, budget, WBS, assignments | 15 to 28 per project |
| Portfolio data | Resource manager, finance | Capacity, allocations, budgets, risks | Not estimated |

- The four activation rules of WSP-14 are met by a starter template once the team is invited. The time goes into three things: a lifecycle that matches how the company really works, the right people with the right roles, and the data that sits in spreadsheets, decks and documents.
- Identity has its own clock: DNS domain verification can take up to 72 hours [Source: S9, Atlassian documentation, accessed 2 October 2026], and SSO needs the customer's IT. Neither belongs on the 30-minute path.
- Published PPM implementations take weeks to months, all as vendor claims: 2 to 6 weeks for Celoxis, 4 to 9 months for enterprise and 12 to 18 months for global rollouts for Planisware, and 6 to 12 months for traditional PPM against 2 to 4 weeks according to monday.com [Source: S8]. No PPM vendor reviewed claims a governed setup in under an hour [Source: S8].
- Microsoft retired Project Online on 30 September 2026; after retirement customers can no longer access their projects in the service [Source: S8, Microsoft 365 Message Center MC1478955 through a mirror, 24 September 2026]. PPM customers with exported plans need a new home now.

# 4. Goal, Users and Principles

## 4.1 Goal and success measure

- **Goal:** any client sets up its company in Metis in 30 minutes, without slide tours and without a long wizard.
- **Success measure:** 30 minutes of hands-on effort by the main setup person until the aha moment: the workspace is active with the company's real lifecycle, real people are invited, the existing projects are in the registry and the executive cockpit shows real data. Deeper data (detailed WBS, capacity, process frameworks) follows, split among the right owners, outside the 30 minutes.
- **Hands-on time:** the time the main setup person (usually the executive, Section 4.2) has the onboarding session open, from the first framing screen to launch, including reading that runs while the session is open; time while the session is paused or closed is not counted (ONB-26).
- **Targets:** Section 19.2.

## 4.2 Users and roles

| User | Part in onboarding | Metis role |
|---|---|---|
| Executive (C-level) | Confirms the framing, drops the files, answers the cards, approves the launch | First tenant admin (TEN-01) and owner of the Draft workspace; Executive |
| Finisher | Named at launch (for example the head of the PMO); default owner of delegated items | Usually Portfolio Manager |
| Owners | Named in the documents: finance for budgets, HR for capacity, each project's PM | Their existing roles |
| Tenant admin | Accepts the AI consent screen, sets masking, switches the setup tool group for external clients | Tenant Admin (often the executive at first) |
| Provider operator | Creates the tenant and records the facts and answers from the sales discovery; sees no business data | Provider Operator |
| Customer IT | Configures SSO, domains and provisioning after launch | Tenant Admin or a delegate |

The onboarding AI has no role of its own: it acts as the executive, within the setup tool group (MCP-04).

## 4.3 Principles

These principles join the UX principles of BRD v4.3, Section 4.5.

| Principle | Why |
|---|---|
| Show before you ask | The executive sees their own portfolio, built from their files, before answering anything; the AI setup builders reviewed all preview a draft before committing it [Source: S8, S10]. |
| Never ask what can be read | Every value read from a document keeps its source; only uncertain or contradictory values become questions [Source: S9, S10]. |
| Pre-select the best guess | Defaults shift choices (meta-analysis of 58 studies, d = 0.68); the number of fields matters more than the number of steps in checkout flows [Source: S9]. |
| Start part-done, keep it short, let them resume | A head start on progress raised completion from 19% to 34% in a field experiment; 72% of three-step tours were completed against 16% of seven-step tours (vendor data) [Source: S9]. |
| Ask the right person, not the executive | Nominate, approve and auto-approve at a deadline is used in HR software such as Lattice and Culture Amp; if-then plans raise follow-through (d = .65) [Source: S9]. |
| Ask irreversible things first | ServiceNow warns that the fiscal calendar type cannot change after funds are allocated [Source: S8]. |
| Nothing is live until a person applies it | Plan, review, then apply is the market norm for AI-built configuration [Source: S10], and it matches BR-35. |
| Everything can be undone for a while | Imports can be undone within a window in HubSpot and Linear [Source: S8, S9]. |
| Ask outside-in | Executive questions are about their own view, the decisions they keep and what they need to know; Metis derives the structure. How the company operates comes from the documents or the PMO (S7). |
| Numbers come from the client's data | Amounts and percentages differ per client, so a question never carries one; Metis computes a boundary from the client's data and shows it as a consequence to confirm (S7). |

# 5. Scope, Assumptions and Constraints

## 5.1 In scope for Release 1

The P0 requirements of module M23, ONB-01 to ONB-27 (Section 7): onboarding session; facts pre-filled from the sales discovery; three framing questions; intake of any supported file; exact parsers before AI; the onboarding agent; the MCP setup tool group; provenance and confidence; the Draft workspace as the draft; adoption of in-flight projects; gap engine; question cards and conversation; Portfolio X-ray; dry run and decision boundary; launch with one approval; undo window; delegation; suggestions after launch; questions at the moment of need; rule-based path; bring-your-own-AI path; AI consent and data handling; boundary hardening of the MCP surface; agent guardrails; assurance suites; onboarding metrics; starting packs.

## 5.2 After Release 1

The P1 requirements, ONB-28 to ONB-40: voice; forwarding address; cloud folder; directory read; board pack reproduction; walkthrough of the client's portfolio; pre-boarding from the sales cycle; IT setup link and domain capture; import into an Active workspace; setup party and overnight completion; human concierge mode; MCP prompts and preview in the client's AI; configuration suggestions from usage.

## 5.3 Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Impact if wrong |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| A-08 | An LLM provider meeting the criteria of D-33 (contractual no-training, zero or short retention, regional processing, a data processing agreement, model version pinning) is available for Release 1. | Tenants that refuse the available terms use the rule-based path or their own AI (Sections 9.6, 12). |
| A-09 | Executives hold at least a project list in a spreadsheet or a slide deck; the design partners' documents represent typical inputs (Q-14). | More cards and owner tasks; the aha moment moves later. |
| A-10 | Provider operators capture the pre-filled facts and answers during the sales discovery of the sales-led model (D-27). | The executive states the facts and answers the three questions from scratch, still within the framing step. |

## 5.4 Constraints

- Person-only decisions stay as in BRD v4.3: approvals, decisions, baseline application, deletions, permission and token changes need a person in the application (BR-35).
- Tenant isolation applies to every onboarding data path (TEN-02, BR-33).
- Provisioning is sales-led in Release 1 (D-27).
- Scope follows business need and is not reduced to fit team size (A-07).
- Metis still neither hosts nor trains an LLM; D-32 narrows the out-of-scope line of BRD v4.3, Section 5.2, for onboarding only.

# 6. The Onboarding Journey

## 6.1 Steps

| Step | What the executive does | What Metis does | Design target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame | Confirms the pre-filled facts and the pre-selected answers to the three questions, changes any of them, or says one sentence instead | Sets the scope, the starting pack, the portfolio grouping, the decision routing and the home view; tells the executive which files help most | Under 1 minute |
| Drop | Drops files, pastes, forwards or records a voice note (voice and forwarding are P1) | Starts reading at once; a live feed shows what it finds | 2 to 5 minutes |
| Ask while reading | Answers the cards that appear: irreversible settings, contradictions, launch blockers | Applies ask, assume, default, delegate or defer per item; keeps the cap (10 cards by default) | Overlaps with reading |
| Draft | Sees their own cockpit, registry and approval flow as a draft, plus the Portfolio X-ray | Runs the dry run of the approval flow on three real projects | Around minute 15 |
| Approve and launch | Reviews what will be created, what is assumed and what goes to owners; names who finishes the rest; approves once | Publishes the lifecycle, adopts the projects, activates the workspace, sends invitations, dispatches owner tasks | By minute 30 |
| Delegate the rest | Nothing, or reassigns an owner | Sends pre-filled tasks with due dates; asks at the moment of need later | Days, not executive time |

On screen the executive sees four steps: Frame, Drop (reading and the first cards), Draft (the remaining cards, the approval flow and the projects to adopt) and Launch; delegation runs after launch.

## 6.2 Facts pre-filled from the sales discovery

In Release 1 the provider operator creates the tenant (TEN-01) and records these facts from the sales conversations, together with the answers to the three questions of 6.3 when the sales discovery gave them; the executive confirms them in one tap or changes any of them (ONB-02).

| Fact | Example (wireframe 46) | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | All of Nova Energy | Workspace boundary and number of workspaces |
| Main kind of work | Engineering, construction and capital projects | Starting pack (ONB-27), MVP objects on or off (MVP-04) |
| Reporting currency | EUR | Irreversible settings, confirmed first |
| Fiscal year | January to December | Irreversible settings, confirmed first |

## 6.3 The three executive questions

| Question | Answers offered, in the executive's voice | What Metis derives |
|---|---|---|
| How do you want to look at your portfolio? | By business unit or subsidiary; by product or service; by client; by strategic objective; by market or region; "Suggest one from my documents" | Portfolio and program levels (BRD v4.3, Section 7.1), cockpit grouping, roadmap lanes |
| How involved do you want to be in project decisions? | "I approve every project before it starts, and any major change"; "I decide only the big or strategic projects; my team handles the rest"; "Our executive committee decides together; I am one member"; "I don't approve projects one by one; tell me when something needs me" | Approvers per approval point and whether a committee with a quorum is used (GOV-03, GOV-05); a rule routing big or strategic projects to the executive (GOV-06), with the boundary computed from the client's data (ONB-14); the executive's place in My approvals (OVW-09) or only in the attention queue (EXE-02); routing of major changes (CHG-10, raised to P0 in Section 13) |
| What do you want to know first every morning? | Where the money goes and whether it matches our priorities; which projects may slip or overrun; whether we have the people for what we committed; what is waiting for my decision | Home view and cockpit order; which data Metis reads and asks for first; which freshness thresholds are set first (BRD v4.3, Section 12.5) |

Each answer previews the resulting home screen. One sentence may replace the three, for example: "I want to see it by subsidiary, I only decide the big bets, and every morning I want to know what is about to slip." At launch Metis asks "Who will finish the rest for you?", suggesting a person from the documents; that person becomes the default owner of delegated items.

## 6.4 Rules

- **Ask outside-in** and **no preset numbers in questions** (Section 4.3). Without budget data, the boundary of big projects goes to the data owner as a delegated item, and launch proceeds with "strategic projects only" as the assumed rule.
- **At most three framing questions**, one tap each, each with "let Metis work it out", on the same screen as the drop zone.
- **Questions appear while reading**, irreversible and launch-blocking items first.
- **Launch never waits for a delegated answer.** What launch needs is answered by the executive, assumed with a visible badge, or set to a safe default; owners confirm or correct after launch.

## 6.5 A 30-minute session

The wireframes follow one illustrative session (sample data, not a measurement). Nova Energy (the tenant created in wireframe 07) is set up on 5 October 2026 by its COO, Rosa Okafor:

| Time | Event | Wireframe |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:48 | Rosa confirms the four pre-filled facts and the three pre-selected answers | 46 |
| 0:48 to 4:00 | She drops seven files: the portfolio tracker, the PMO handbook, the ExCo pack, the Capex plan, the org chart, an MS Project schedule and a zip of twelve status reports | 46, 47 |
| 4:00 to 14:00 | Metis reads; she answers six cards and three go to owners | 47 |
| 14:00 | The draft cockpit shows 34 projects in 4 business units, EUR 214.6M; the X-ray finds eight kinds of problem | 48 |
| 14:00 to 24:00 | She checks the approval flow and its dry run, changes one approver in the conversation and leaves the last cards open, so their values stay assumed; 14 projects will come to her; 34 projects will be adopted, 21 of them committed | 49, 50, 51 |
| 24:00 to 27:00 | She names Sam Varga to finish the rest and approves the launch | 52 |
| Days after | 31 items go to 6 owners, due 12 October 2026; 12 are closed by 7 October | 53 |
````

````markdown
# 9. Reading, Conversion and the Draft

## 9.1 Pipeline

| Step | Component | Uses the LLM | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Receive | Intake: upload and paste, and after Release 1 forward and voice (P1); tenant-scoped storage with malware scanning (PLT-07) | No | Stored inputs |
| Extract | Parsers per format: spreadsheet cells with formatting and colours, CSV, MS Project XML and MPP, Word, PDF (text, and OCR for scans), PowerPoint text and tables, saved emails; images and audio go to the provider's vision and speech services | Images and audio only | Source fragments with stable IDs (file, sheet, cell, page, slide, time) |
| Understand | Onboarding agent: the third-party LLM, run by a Metis onboarding service, reads fragments as quoted data with the framing answers and the starting pack as context; maps columns, resolves entities, matches the operating model, finds contradictions | Yes | Proposals sent through the setup tools (Section 7.1) |
| Validate and write | Metis MCP server: schema, permission, tenant and business-rule checks; writes into the Draft workspace and the onboarding session; returns errors written for self-correction | No | Draft records, questions, findings |
| Review and launch | The product's own screens on the Draft workspace; question cards; launch summary | No | Live workspace |

Exact parsing comes first: a structured input whose mapping is unambiguous is read without the LLM (ONB-05). The LLM decides ambiguous mappings, reads unstructured content, resolves entities and matches the operating model.

## 9.2 The Draft workspace is the draft

BRD v4.3 already has a non-live state for a new workspace; the design reuses it instead of a separate staging copy of every entity (ONB-09).

- The workspace is created in Draft (WSP-05): only owners and admins open it; members do not see it.
- The lifecycle is a draft version (GOV-19 to GOV-21), published at launch.
- Option lists and the portfolio tree are written to the Draft workspace.
- People become member records with proposed roles; invitations and role grants take effect at launch, when the executive approves (PLT-03, BR-35).
- Existing projects are adopted into the Draft workspace (9.3).
- The onboarding session (ONB-01) holds what BRD v4.3 lacks: framing answers, inputs, source fragments, per-field provenance and confidence, questions, delegated items, findings, the batch ID on every created record, and each item's status.
- The draft shown to the executive is the product itself: the cockpit and the registry of the Draft workspace, with badges from the session.
- "Start over" deletes every record the batch created in the Draft workspace; the audit log and the session's inputs remain. After launch, the undo window (ONB-16) removes the batch's unchanged records and lists the others.
- After launch the AI no longer writes records: a setup call that carries a source is stored as a suggestion in the session, and the responsible person accepts it (ONB-18).

A separate staging layer, holding proposed records outside the product and applying them as a change set, was considered and not kept: it mirrors patterns that protect live systems [Source: S10, Stripe and ServiceNow], whereas a new Metis workspace is not live until activation, and a second model of every entity would double the work and let the preview drift from the product. Importing into a workspace that is already Active is a different case, planned after Release 1 (ONB-36).

## 9.3 Adopting in-flight projects

CHR-17 creates every project in Draft with a setup checklist. Onboarding brings projects that are already running, so the addendum adds an adoption path (ONB-10):

- A project is adopted at its current stage, read from the documents or asked. Earlier stages are recorded as completed before Metis, with the source document as evidence. No gate decision is fabricated (BR-46); the Decision Log gets one entry per project: "Adopted at stage X at launch, approved by" the executive.
- When the documents show an approved budget and dates, the project is adopted as committed and its baseline is captured at launch from the imported values (CHG-06), labelled "from import" (BR-47). Otherwise it stays uncommitted and change control is advisory (BR-04).
- Mandatory artifacts of stages completed before adoption are not demanded retroactively; exit rules (BR-17) apply from the adoption stage onward. A committed project without an owner or a sponsor is still adopted as committed: the gap becomes a delegated item and an attention item until the person is named, instead of blocking the adoption (BR-01; Section 13, CHR-17 row).
- Declared status and health from the tracker are kept as the last known status with the document's as-of time. Computed metrics (BRD v4.3, Section 12) show "not available yet" until a plan is imported, as partial data under BR-39.
- The executive's single launch approval covers the adoption of every listed project.

## 9.4 Provenance and confidence

- Every proposed value carries its source fragment (file, location, quoted text), a confidence band (high, medium, low) and a status (read, assumed, default, confirmed, asked, delegated, conflicting) (ONB-08).
- High-confidence values are applied quietly and show their source on hover; medium values are applied with a "check" badge, and a "check" value still unconfirmed at launch counts as assumed; low-confidence and conflicting values become questions.
- "Assumed" and "default" badges stay visible after launch until someone confirms the value, and the value appears in the responsible owner's attention list; the executive's attention queue (EXE-02) shows the assumed values as one item per owner, with the number still to confirm, together with that owner's overdue delegated tasks (ONB-17), until then.
- This addendum fixes the bands and their behaviour; the numeric cut-offs are tuned in Discovery with the design partners.

## 9.5 One pipeline, two drivers

The setup tool group (ONB-07, Section 7.1) is prepare-only: it writes only into a Draft workspace and its onboarding session, never into an Active workspace, and never publishes, activates, invites or grants roles. It is off by default for external clients; a tenant admin switches it on, the pattern of an admin tool group disabled by default [Source: S10, Atlassian Rovo MCP server]. Every proposal carries source references, a confidence per field and an idempotency key (PLT-06), and returns what was written plus any validation errors.

The Metis onboarding agent calls the same MCP server as any client, with a short-lived onboarding token bound to the executive, the tenant, the Draft workspace and the setup tool group. On the second path (Section 12) the client's own AI uses the same tools with the same kind of token, bound to the person who creates it.

## 9.6 Rule-based path

When the tenant does not enable the onboarding AI, structured inputs go through column-mapping screens (suggestions by header names, a kept-and-dropped report) and produce the same proposals; unstructured documents are not read; the question cards, the launch and the delegation work the same way (ONB-20).

# 10. Questions, Delegation and Launch

## 10.1 What counts as missing

The onboarding session checks the Draft workspace against five rule sets and turns every gap into one item (ONB-11):

| Rule set | Examples of gaps | Source of the rule |
|---|---|---|
| Activation | No published default lifecycle; a status without a system state; no portfolio | WSP-14, BR-14 |
| Publish check | An approval point without approvers; a quorum the named approvers cannot reach; a stage without an owner role | GOV-21 |
| Adoption | A project's current stage unknown; committed without budget or dates; committed without owner or sponsor | Section 9.3, BR-01, BR-03 |
| The executive's answers | The boundary of big or strategic projects; the members of the executive committee; the data the chosen home view needs | Section 6.3 |
| Feature data | Capacity and allocations, actuals, strategic objectives, process frameworks | RES-03, CHR-13, CHR-15, BLD-09 |

## 10.2 Ask, assume, default, delegate or defer

Each item gets one treatment, decided by three tests: is it needed for launch, how costly is a wrong value, and who knows the answer.

| Treatment | When | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Ask the executive | Needed for launch and only the executive knows, or the value cannot change later | Confirm currency and fiscal year; who sits on the executive committee |
| Assume, with a visible badge | Needed for launch, readable with medium confidence, cheap to correct | A project's current stage inferred from its status report |
| Safe default | Needed for launch, stated nowhere, and the starting pack has a sensible value | Stage owner roles and mandatory artifacts from the starting pack |
| Delegate | Someone named in the documents knows it better than the executive | Budgets to finance; each project's dates to its PM; capacity to HR |
| Defer | Needed neither for launch nor for the chosen home view | Process frameworks; naming the person who approves a late approval point, asked when the first project gets there (the people holding the starting pack's role approve until then) |

- The executive sees at most 10 cards in the 30-minute path (a product setting, 10 by default), ordered: irreversible settings, launch blockers, what the chosen home view needs, the rest. Items beyond the cap are assumed, defaulted or delegated automatically and listed on the launch summary.
- A question never carries a preset number, and launch never waits for a delegated answer (Section 6.4).

## 10.3 Question cards and the conversation panel

- **Card:** one question in business words; Metis's best guess pre-selected with its source (quoted passage and file); alternatives; "Use this" (accept the guess, marked assumed, or confirmed when only the executive knows the answer); "Ask someone" (delegate, with the suggested owner pre-filled). Target: under 15 seconds per card.
- **Bulk card:** "We matched 78 of 86 people to roles; check the 8 we are unsure about."
- **Contradiction card:** both sources side by side; pick one or type the right value.
- **Conversation panel:** free text, and voice where enabled (ONB-28). The agent turns an answer into proposals and states what changed, for example "Added Finance as an approver for the 11 largest projects."
- Cards appear while documents are still being read.

## 10.4 Portfolio X-ray

Findings from the client's own documents, shown next to the draft and turned into attention items (EXE-02) at launch (ONB-13):

| Finding | Example | Suggested owner |
|---|---|---|
| Missing accountability | Committed projects without an owner or a sponsor (BR-01) | PMO |
| No strategic link | Projects linked to no objective, when objectives are known (BR-02) | Executive |
| Conflicting figures | A budget or a date that differs between two documents | Data owner |
| Slipped dates | A target date that moved between two versions of a status report | Project manager |
| Possible duplicates | Two similar projects in different units | PMO |
| Overloaded people | One person leading or delivering many projects (count-based, as OVW-03) | Resource manager |
| Stale status | A last status older than the freshness threshold (BRD v4.3, Section 12.5) | Project manager |
| Suspicious content | Text in a document that reads like instructions to an AI | Tenant admin |

## 10.5 Delegation

- **Owners:** the person named at launch to finish the rest (default owner) and the owners found in the documents (each project's PM, finance for budgets, HR for capacity) (ONB-17).
- **Task:** pre-filled values with their sources; accept all, edit, reassign or "I don't know"; a due date and reminders; correcting a value that a baseline from import has locked opens a change request (BR-47). Channels in Release 1: the in-app task list and email (D-16); chat channels follow BRD v4.3.
- Owners are members of the workspace and receive the normal invitation at launch (PLT-03).
- **Auto-accept at the due date applies only to values already applied at launch** (assumed or defaulted): the badge changes to "kept by default" and the item stays in the default owner's attention list. A suggestion that would change data after launch never applies itself (BR-48).
- **Escalation:** an overdue task goes to the default owner, then to the executive's attention queue (EXE-02); the morning digest (PLT-10, P1 in BRD v4.3) carries the same line once it is enabled.
- **Progress per feature:** for example "Investment view: 9 of 12 budgets confirmed"; until setup is complete the executive's home shows a slim completeness bar.

## 10.6 Approve and launch

The launch summary is one page in business words (ONB-15):

- **What will be created:** workspaces, portfolios and programs, projects adopted (by stage, committed or not), people invited (by role), the approval flow (one line per approval point) and the X-ray findings.
- **What is assumed or defaulted:** count and the most important items.
- **What goes to owners:** per owner, the number of items and the due date.
- **Who finishes the rest:** suggested from the documents, editable.
- **Readiness:** the WSP-14 activation rules, the GOV-21 publish check and the dry run, each passed or failed with its failure in plain words and a one-click fix.

**Dry run** (ONB-14): three adopted projects chosen to exercise the most rules (the largest by budget, one routed to the executive, one typical) run through the drafted approval flow; the screen shows who approves each point, whether the named approvers can reach the quorum and which documents become mandatory.

One "Approve and launch", by the executive, who is the first tenant admin (TEN-01) and the owner of the Draft workspace unless another owner was named, runs on the server in one transaction:

1. Re-runs every readiness check; any failure stops the launch and nothing changes.
2. Publishes the lifecycle draft. The AI is the author of the draft and the executive its reviewer, which satisfies the review step of GOV-21.
3. Adopts the projects (Section 9.3): stage instances, baselines from import for committed projects, one Decision Log entry per project.
4. Activates the workspace (WSP-05).
5. Grants the approved roles and queues the invitations, which are sent only after the launch commits, so a rolled-back launch sends none (PLT-03, BR-35).
6. Dispatches the owner tasks and turns the X-ray findings into attention items.
7. Records every step in the audit log: the AI as author of each proposal, the executive as approver, channel "onboarding" (PLT-11, MCP-11).

After launch, an undo window (14 days by default, set per tenant, D-35) removes the batch's records that nobody has changed since and lists those it keeps, together with any unchanged record a kept one depends on; audit and Decision Log entries stay (ONB-16).

## 10.7 Effort budget

- The 30 minutes belong to the executive and are measured (ONB-26).
- Owner effort is measured separately, with design targets such as "a PM confirms their own adopted project in under 5 minutes" and "finance confirms a budget list in one pass".

# 11. Guardrails and AI Policy

Principle stated by the product owner (S7): **the data belongs to the customer.** Any user may read and act on what their roles allow, in the application or through MCP with any client the tenant's policy admits (MCP-20), including to make Metis do what they want. The security work is on the boundary: MCP exposes nothing that lets anyone reach beyond it. The boundary is enforced by architecture and code on the server, never by a prompt; OWASP states that critical controls must not be delegated to the LLM and that sensitive information must not sit in system prompts [Source: S11, LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage].

## 11.1 The boundary

| Inside: available to a user through the app or MCP | Outside: never exposed through any channel |
|---|---|
| Records of their own tenant that their roles allow, intersected with the token's scopes (MCP-04) | Any record, name, count or even the existence of another tenant (TEN-02, BR-33) |
| Figures computed by Metis, with as-of time and metric version (MCP-10, BR-39) | Database names, table and column names, query language, raw queries |
| The published tool list, schemas and versions (MCP-09) | Internal hostnames, service topology, software versions beyond the MCP protocol version, stack traces |
| Their own audit entries and MCP activity; all of the tenant's for tenant admins (MCP-11) | Signing keys, provider keys, token hashes, other users' tokens (BR-36) |
| Drafts and proposals they or their AI create (setup tool group, prepare tools) | The prompts and orchestration of Metis's own onboarding agent |
| Business-level errors that say what to fix (MCP-15) | Actions reserved to a person in the application: approvals, decisions, baseline application, deletions, permission and token changes (BR-35) |

Inside the tenant the data belongs to the organization, not to each user: roles still decide who sees what, and the onboarding agent acts as the executive and sees what the executive sees. BR-35 is unchanged; it is the customer's own governance (AI prepares, people decide, a positioning point of BRD v4.3, Section 4.2), not a limit on access to their data.

Threat classes considered, from the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 [Source: S11]: prompt injection (LLM01), sensitive information disclosure (LLM02), improper output handling (LLM05), excessive agency (LLM06), system prompt leakage (LLM07), misinformation (LLM09), unbounded consumption (LLM10).

## 11.2 Hardening the MCP surface against tricks

The same surface serves the customer's own AI clients and Metis's onboarding agent, so one set of controls protects both (ONB-23).

| Trick | Control |
|---|---|
| Probing for other tenants by guessing identifiers or names | Opaque identifiers; one response for "not found" and "no access"; the token's tenant audience checked on every call (TEN-02) |
| Asking for more than the role allows | Every tool runs the same server-side permission checks as the application (PLT-04, MCP-04) |
| Smuggling a query or code | No generic query, search-anything or execute tool; every parameter validated against its schema and allow-lists; page-size caps (MCP-13) |
| Making the server fetch an address (server-side request forgery) | No tool fetches a URL supplied by a client; a cloud folder is read only through a connector the tenant admin authorizes with the cloud provider (ONB-30) |
| Reading internals from errors | Errors carry a category and a fix, never a stack trace, a query or an internal name |
| Instructions hidden in record text or documents | Stored text is returned as data and never interpreted as instructions by the server (MCP-16); write tools act only on explicit parameters; every setup proposal cites sources that exist in its session |
| Changing what a tool claims to do | Tool names, descriptions and schemas are static and versioned (MCP-09) and contain no secrets or internal hints |
| Writing outside the draft or taking person-only actions | The setup tool group writes only into a Draft workspace; publishing, activation, invitations and role grants need a person (BR-35, BR-43, BR-44) |
| Exhausting the service | Rate limits and quotas per token and per tenant (MCP-12, TEN-10) |

## 11.3 Metis's own onboarding agent

The agent is one more client of the same surface, so 11.1 and 11.2 already bound it. Because its prompt and orchestration are Metis internals and it calls a third-party LLM, it adds these controls (ONB-24):

- **Nothing worth stealing in its context:** task instructions and published schemas only; no credentials, hostnames, provider keys, database names or permission structure; provider keys stay in the onboarding service.
- **An internals lock, not a topic lock:** it answers anything about the customer's data that the executive may see within its onboarding token (Section 9.5), and refuses only Metis internals, other tenants and requests unrelated to the customer's business, with the fixed reply of 11.6. An input classifier flags probing; repeated probing slows the session and notifies the tenant admin.
- **Documents as data:** text reaches the model inside marked data blocks with its source; each document is read in its own pass where possible, so one hostile file cannot steer the reading of the others; instruction-like text is removed and reported as a Portfolio X-ray finding.
- **Output screening by code outside the model:** each reply is checked for canary strings planted in the prompt, key and token formats, internal hostnames and other tenants' names; a hit blocks the reply and records a security event. Output is rendered as text, never executed or inserted as markup.
- **Spend:** quotas on files, pages, AI calls and, once voice is enabled, audio minutes per onboarding, and a provider spend cap per tenant.
- **Audit:** every AI call, tool call, refusal and security event is in the tenant audit log (MCP-11, PLT-11); what is kept follows D-34.

## 11.4 Proof before release

Three suites run on every release and on every change of model, provider or prompt, like the tenant isolation suite (TEN-02), and their reports are kept as release evidence (ONB-25):

- **Boundary suite:** cross-tenant probing with a second test tenant, identifier enumeration, access beyond role for each role (generated from the permission matrix, BRD v4.3 Section 18.4), parameter fuzzing, attempts at server-side fetches, inspection of every error message for internals, rate limits. Pass: zero data or existence of another tenant, zero access beyond role, zero internals in any response.
- **Agent red-team suite:** direct injection; injection hidden in each supported file type (spreadsheet cell, slide note, PDF text layer, image text, audio); system prompt extraction; role-play and multi-turn jailbreaks; attacks in Vietnamese and other languages; spend exhaustion. Pass: zero canary or secret leaks, zero writes outside the Draft workspace and its onboarding session, zero person-only actions by the AI.
- **Extraction-accuracy suite:** reference documents with the records a person extracted from them (projects, people, budgets, dates, stages); precision and recall per record type, against the threshold of D-39. It guards against wrong values (LLM09) as the other suites guard against attacks.

OWASP lists adversarial testing that treats the model as an untrusted user among the mitigations of prompt injection [Source: S11, LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection].

## 11.5 Data handling: the customer decides

- **Off until enabled.** Because the data is the customer's, Metis sends nothing to the third-party LLM until a tenant admin enables it on the consent screen (ONB-22). In the sales-led flow the provider may pre-select "on"; the executive, as first tenant admin, still accepts it explicitly.
- **The consent screen states** which provider processes the content and in which region, what is sent (the fragments needed, the questions and answers, never other tenants' data), that the provider does not train on customer data, the provider's retention, what Metis keeps, how to switch the AI off, and the rule-based path as the alternative.
- **Masking is the customer's choice:** sensitive personal fields beyond names, titles and work email (for example salaries or private phone numbers in a capacity sheet) are masked before sending by default; the tenant admin can switch masking off or extend it.
- **Sub-processors:** the LLM provider and any speech or vision service join the published sub-processor list (BRD v4.3, Section 17, data lifecycle).
- **Inputs kept by Metis:** uploaded files are the customer's documents in their own tenant storage, kept as the source behind provenance links under the tenant's retention policy, with an option to delete them after launch (provenance then keeps the file name and quoted passage only, D-38).
- **Transparency:** the agent always presents itself as AI (the square "AI" avatar of the wireframes), and every record it proposed shows "proposed by AI, approved by" the person. Where the EU AI Act applies, Article 50(1) requires informing people that they are interacting with an AI system, from 2 August 2026 [Source: S12] [Unverified - confirm applicability to Metis with counsel, Q-16].
- **Model changes:** the provider and model version are recorded per session; a new model or provider is used only after the three suites pass.
- **The provider's name is not a secret:** the sub-processor list and the consent screen name it; what stays protected is listed in 11.1.
- **What the audit keeps for onboarding AI calls** (D-34): metadata and redacted excerpts by default; the full prompt and reply only for calls flagged as security events, for 90 days, visible to the tenant admin. This mirrors open question Q-12 of BRD v4.3 for MCP calls.

## 11.6 The fixed reply to probing

"I can help with anything about your company's data in Metis, but I can't share how I am built or anything about the systems behind Metis. Shall we continue with *the current step*?" Shown in the user's language; the same reply for every out-of-scope request, so probing learns nothing from variations.

# 12. Bring Your Own AI

## 12.1 Who it is for

- Tenants that keep the Metis onboarding AI switched off (policy, compliance, procurement).
- Teams whose own AI already reaches their documents: an enterprise assistant connected to the company's file stores can find and read files the executive would never upload, which makes this path richer, not only a fallback [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Anyone who prefers to work from the AI client they use every day.

## 12.2 How it works

1. **Enable:** the tenant admin switches on the setup tool group for MCP clients (off by default, Section 9.5); the tenant's client allowlist applies (MCP-20).
2. **Connect:** the executive or a delegate opens "Set up with your own AI". The page extends the AI access page (MCP-15, wireframe 08) with the endpoint, OAuth or an onboarding token limited to the setup tools and the Draft workspace (7 days by default, never above the tenant maximum), and a test call (ONB-21).
3. **Ask:** the user pastes one short prompt. The intelligence is served by Metis, not by the prompt: the first call, `get_setup_context`, returns the framing answers, the starting pack, the record schemas, the order of work, the rules (cite a source for every value, never invent, raise a question instead of guessing) and the session's open questions. Prompts stay short, work in any language and follow Metis's changes without anyone editing what they pasted.
4. **Work:** the client's AI reads the files in the user's environment and calls the same setup tools as Metis's agent; validation errors come back in words the AI can act on.
5. **Watch:** the Metis tab shows the same live feed, draft screens, cards and X-ray as Section 6, for example "Your AI added 34 projects and raised 6 questions".
6. **Launch in Metis only:** the launch summary and the single approval happen in the application (Section 10.6). The client's AI can never launch, invite or grant roles (BR-35).

## 12.3 The prompt pack

| Job | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Set up from documents | "Use the Metis tools to set up our company from these files. Start with get_setup_context and follow it." |
| Import a project list | "Add the projects in this file to our Metis setup, with their owners, dates, budgets and status." |
| Describe how we approve projects | "From this handbook, describe in Metis how our projects get approved and who approves them." |
| Add our people | "Add the people in this org chart to our Metis setup with their titles and suggested roles." |
| Fill in budgets | "Fill in the budgets of our Metis projects from this finance sheet." |
| Answer open questions | "Get the open Metis setup questions and answer the ones these files can answer by proposing the values with the setup tools; leave the others." |

Release 1 ships the pack as copy-ready text on the page and in the guide, in the user's language. Serving the same prompts as MCP prompts follows MCP-17 (P1 in BRD v4.3, ONB-39), so this P0 path does not depend on a P1 requirement. A user who keeps the setup context can also ask freely, for example "Our PMO handbook is in the shared drive; read it and set up our approval flow".

## 12.4 Data, quality and safety on this path

- **Data:** files are read by the customer's AI in the customer's environment; Metis receives only the proposals and the quoted sources. Metis's LLM provider is not involved; the customer's provider processes the data under the customer's own terms (BRD v4.3, Section 17).
- **Provenance:** the client reports file name, location and quoted passage for each value; Metis records them in the session as "reported by your AI", so proposals can cite them (ONB-07), and does not hold the file.
- **Quality:** Metis validation catches structural errors (an approval point without approvers, a missing stage), not wrong values; the same badges, cards and launch review apply. The verified-client list (MCP-15) gains a "verified for onboarding" mark for clients that pass Metis's onboarding test scenario.
- **Safety:** the guide advises running Metis setup without other connectors that can send data elsewhere (web, email) in the same session, following vendor guidance on prompt injection across MCP servers [Source: S10]; the boundary of Section 11 holds whatever the client does.
- **When IT blocks external MCP connections** (a case Stripe documents [Source: S10, Stripe MCP documentation]): the rule-based path, or the Metis onboarding AI if the tenant enables it.
````

````markdown
# 16. Delivery

- **Workstream "Onboarding and intake"**, from Discovery onward, beside the seven workstreams of BRD v4.3, staffed from the agency team of A-07; the split of the team across streams is set in Discovery (BRD v4.3, 18.2).
- **Discovery** delivers: the reference document sets of the design partners (Q-14) and the extraction-accuracy threshold (D-39); the provider selection (D-33); the list of starting packs (D-36); a prototype of the framing and draft screens tested with executives in the UX phase (BRD v4.3, 18.4).
- **Milestone 1A:** onboarding session, intake and exact parsers, the onboarding agent, the setup tool group, the Draft workspace, adoption of projects, cards, launch with the registry (the registry, M16, integrates at 1B like the cockpit) and the approval flow (its routing of big or strategic projects uses the conditional flow of GOV-06, which BRD v4.3 integrates at 1B, so the dry run of ONB-14 completes at 1B), the rule-based path, consent, boundary hardening and the three suites.
- **Milestone 1B:** the draft cockpit (the cockpit, M15, integrates at 1B), the Portfolio X-ray as attention items, delegation at full scope, the bring-your-own-AI path with its verified clients, onboarding metrics, the dry run of ONB-14 on projects routed by the conditional flow.
- **Pilot readiness:** the three suites pass; the acceptance list of Section 19.1 passes with the design partners; the targets of Section 19.2 are met, or the variance explained.

Every other P0 requirement of M23 is complete at Pilot readiness, as BRD v4.3 requires for every P0 requirement (BRD v4.3, 18.2).

# 18. Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|----------------------------------------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| Wrong extraction paints a wrong portfolio | High | Sources on every value, badges, accuracy suite, launch review, undo window |
| Over-trust in baselines taken from documents | Medium | "From import" label; change requests as for any baseline (BR-47) |
| LLM provider outage, change or price rise | Medium | Rule-based path; model version pinning; suites before any change; provider criteria (D-33) |
| AI cost exceeds what the price allows | Medium | Quotas, spend caps, exact parsers first (Q-18) |
| Personal data in uploaded documents | High | Consent, masking by default, sub-processor list, retention settings |
| Executives still drop off | High | Metrics per step (ONB-26); usability tests with design partners in the UX phase |
| Owners ignore delegated tasks | Medium | Launch never waits; escalation; launch values kept by default |
| Release 1 grows | Medium | Own workstream; milestone placement of Section 16; P1 requirements stay out of Release 1 |

# 19. Acceptance Checklist and Onboarding Targets

## 19.1 Acceptance checklist

- From a tenant with pre-filled facts and a reference document set, an executive reaches the draft cockpit and then launches within the targets of 19.2, measured in moderated sessions with the design partners.
- The framing screen has three questions, none with a preset number, each skippable; the one-sentence answer sets the same values.
- Each supported input type is read; the kept-and-dropped report lists what was ignored and why; an MS Project or Project Online export becomes WBS items with dates and dependencies.
- Every value created by onboarding shows its source, or an "assumed" or "default" label.
- The executive sees no more cards than the cap; every other gap is assumed, defaulted, delegated or deferred and listed on the launch summary.
- In-flight projects are adopted at their current stage with their history before Metis; committed ones get a baseline from import; no gate decision is fabricated.
- Approve and launch runs the seven steps in one transaction; a failing check blocks the launch and names its fix.
- Undo within the window removes the batch's records that nobody changed and lists the others.
- Delegated tasks reach their owners; auto-accept keeps only values applied at launch; a suggestion after launch applies only when a person accepts it.
- A verified client sets up a Draft workspace from the prompt pack; launch happens only in Metis.
- With the onboarding AI switched off, the rule-based path sets up a workspace from structured files.
- The boundary, red-team and extraction-accuracy suites pass their criteria (Section 11.4).
- No customer content reaches the LLM provider before consent; masking is on by default.
- Every AI call, tool call, refusal and security event is in the tenant audit log.

## 19.2 Onboarding targets (proposed, to confirm with the design partners in Discovery)

| Measure | Proposed target |
|---|---|
| Executive hands-on time to the draft cockpit | 15 minutes or less (median) |
| Executive hands-on time to launch | 30 minutes or less (median) |
| Cards answered by the executive | 10 or fewer (median) |
| Values read with high confidence, assumed or defaulted, asked | Tracked; no target before the pilot |
| Values corrected within 14 days of launch | Tracked as the accuracy signal; target after the pilot |
| Delegated items closed by their due date | 80% or more |
| Onboarding sessions abandoned before launch | Tracked per step; target after the pilot |
| PM time to confirm their own adopted project | 5 minutes or less (median) |
| Days from launch to setup complete | Tracked |
````
