# Appendix A. Glossary Additions

| Term | Meaning |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Adoption (of a project) | Bringing a running project into Metis at its current stage, with earlier stages recorded as completed before Metis and, when committed, a baseline from import (ONB-10) |
| Assumed value | A value applied without confirmation because launch needs it: inferred with medium confidence, accepted from a card (a value only the executive knows is confirmed instead), or set by a stated fallback rule; it keeps a badge until someone confirms it |
| Bring your own AI | The second onboarding path: the client's own LLM client reads its files and calls the setup tools (Section 12) |
| Default value | A value taken from the starting pack because no document states it; shown with a badge until confirmed |
| Draft workspace | A workspace in the Draft state of WSP-05; during onboarding it holds the whole draft that the executive reviews and launches |
| Dry run | A rehearsal of the drafted approval flow on three adopted projects before launch (ONB-14) |
| Finisher | The person the executive names at launch to finish the rest; default owner of delegated items |
| Framing questions | The three outside-in questions to the executive: how they look at the portfolio, how involved they want to be in decisions, what they want to know first (Section 6.3) |
| Kept by default | The state of a value applied at launch that nobody confirmed by its due date; the value stays and the item remains in the finisher's attention list (BR-48) |
| Onboarding session | The record of one onboarding: facts, answers, inputs, provenance, questions, tasks, findings and the batch ID of everything it created (ONB-01) |
| Onboarding token | A short-lived token limited to the setup tools and one Draft workspace (ONB-21) |
| Portfolio X-ray | Findings drawn from the client's own documents during onboarding, such as missing sponsors or conflicting budgets (ONB-13) |
| Provenance | The source of a value (file, location and quoted passage) with a confidence band and a status (ONB-08) |
| Rule-based path | Onboarding without the AI: exact parsers and column mapping (ONB-20) |
| Setup tool group | The prepare-only MCP tools that write proposals into a Draft workspace and its session (Section 7.1) |
| Starting pack | A provider-maintained lifecycle, option lists, process frameworks and approval flow for one kind of work; the reference Metis matches documents against (ONB-27) |
| Suggestion | After launch, a change proposed by the AI or an MCP client that applies only when a person accepts it (ONB-18) |

# Appendix C. Options Considered

Sixty-three options were assessed (S13). This appendix records the approaches compared and where each group of options landed.

## C.1 Three approaches

| Criterion | Draft first (kept) | Conversation first | Delegate first |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executive time to the draft cockpit | About 15 minutes (target) | 20 to 30 minutes, depending on the conversation | Not in the first session; after owners answer |
| Feels like | Seeing my company in the product, then fixing by exception | Talking to a consultant | Assigning a project to my team |
| Reviewing 30 projects and 80 people | Fast: tables and bulk confirmation in context | Slow: long lists do not fit a conversation | Fast for the executive, slow overall |
| Risk of drop-off | Low: value appears before any effort | Medium: long conversations tire | High: momentum depends on others |
| Data accuracy | High: sources shown, owners asked for the uncertain items | Medium: one person's memory | Highest: owners answer for their own data |
| Fit with BR-35 and GOV-21 | One draft, one approval in the application | Many small approvals inside a conversation | Many approvals by many people |

The catalogue (S13) also compared build effort. That criterion is not repeated here: its rating for "draft first" assumed a separate draft layer across entities, and the approved design keeps the draft in the Draft workspace instead (Section 9.2).

The product owner kept "draft first", added the framing questions of "conversation first" before the drop and the owner tasks of "delegate first" after launch, with three fixes: at most three framing questions, questions while reading, and a launch that never waits for delegated answers (S7).

## C.2 Where the options landed

| Group | Kept for Release 1 | After Release 1 | Not kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| Getting data in | Drop and paste anything; photos and screenshots; exports from current tools; bring your own AI (ONB-04, ONB-05, ONB-21) | Voice note, forwarding address, cloud folder, directory, pre-boarding (ONB-28 to ONB-31, ONB-34); public company documents, meeting recordings and calendar reading, with no requirement yet (consent risk for recordings, S10) | None |
| Reading and converting | Two-lane reading, sources on every value, confidence bands, entity resolution, contradictions, status and colour translation, operating model from documents, closest reference model, plans to WBS, kept-and-dropped report, suspicious content flag (ONB-05, ONB-06, ONB-08, ONB-13, ONB-20, ONB-27) | Capacity and budget sheets beyond what launch needs, charters from contracts, with no requirement yet | None |
| Value before setup | Draft shown as the product; Portfolio X-ray (ONB-09, ONB-13) | Board pack reproduction; walkthrough of the client's portfolio (ONB-32, ONB-33); next-quarter preview, with no requirement yet | None |
| Asking only what is missing | Ask, assume, default, delegate or defer; one-tap cards; bulk confirmation; ask the owner; conversation; card cap; questions at the moment of need (ONB-11, ONB-12, ONB-17, ONB-19) | Voice answers (ONB-28); answers by email, with no requirement yet | None |
| People and access | Identity off the critical path; people from documents; placeholders (ONB-09, ONB-17) | IT setup link and domain capture (ONB-35) | None |
| Operating model | Approval flow in business words; dry run; starting packs (ONB-14, ONB-27) | None | None |
| Safety and trust | Draft held in the Draft workspace (the catalogue's Setup Plan); undo window; guardrails; consent; short-lived tokens (ONB-09, ONB-16, ONB-21 to ONB-25) | None | A separate staging layer (Section 9.2) |
| Bring your own AI path | Prompt pack and guide as copy-ready text; errors written for the LLM (ONB-21, ONB-07) | Preview inside the client's AI and the prompt pack served as MCP prompts (ONB-39) | None |
| After launch | Owner tasks; onboarding metrics (ONB-17, ONB-26) | Configuration suggestions from usage (ONB-40) | None |
| Wild cards | None | Setup party and overnight completion; human concierge (ONB-37, ONB-38); onboarding without opening Metis, with no requirement yet | A fully automatic launch (contradicts BR-35; S10) |

# GPT review prompt: BRD addendum "Onboarding in 30 minutes"

This file has two parts. Part 1 is for the sender: which files to attach and how to send them. Part 2 is the prompt: copy it verbatim from the line "PROMPT START" to the line "PROMPT END" and paste it into the ChatGPT chat box.

- `design/option-catalogue.md`: the 63 options that were weighed, each with its ruling.
- `research/research-competitors.md`, `research/research-onboarding-patterns.md`, `research/research-ai-onboarding.md`: market research notes; every claim has a URL and a date.

## Part 2. Prompt

---- PROMPT START ----

# Role

You are an independent review panel of four experts working together as one team:

1. A business analyst and PMO expert with many years of implementing project portfolio management (PPM) software and B2B SaaS.
2. A UX lead for enterprise software, specializing in onboarding and in the experience of C-level leaders.
3. A solution architect for multi-tenant SaaS and LLM integration through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
4. An AI application security expert: prompt injection, data leaks, the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications.

Task: review the BRD addendum "Onboarding in 30 minutes" and its 12 accompanying wireframes. Challenge it, do not praise it. Every comment must be specific, backed by evidence, and come with a proposal that can actually be done.

# Context

- The product "Metis": Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence & Governance Platform, a multi-tenant SaaS with an MCP server for LLMs. The main BRD is version 4.3, which has been through two of your review rounds.
- The BRD addendum has one goal: every customer can set up their company in 30 minutes of effort from the main setup person, counted up to the "aha moment": the workspace is activated with the real project lifecycle, real people are invited, the existing projects are in the portfolio, and the executive cockpit shows real figures. The deeper parts are done later and handed to the right people.
- Decisions of the product owner (Section 1.2 of the BRD addendum), which must be respected:
  - The main user is a C-level leader with very little time. Questions for the leader are asked from their point of view and hold no preset numbers.
  - Metis does not build or train a model itself. Metis calls a third-party LLM through an API, switched on by the customer; that AI calls Metis's own MCP to create records (D-32).
  - The data belongs to the customer. Security focuses on the boundaries: other customers, the internals of Metis, roles, and the decisions that only a person may make.
  - There is a second path (the customer uses their own AI with Metis's prompt pack) and a path without AI.
  - The development team is about 40 developers (assumption A-07 of the main BRD): do not propose cutting or postponing scope because of team size. You may still propose changing scope for other reasons (value, technical risk, dependencies, legal), in which case the reason must be stated clearly.
- The BRD addendum does not amend BRD 4.3; Section 13 lists 20 changes to be merged in later.
- The automated build has already checked: no duplicate codes; every reference exists in the main BRD or in the addendum; every P0 requirement of the addendum has at least one wireframe; every requirement code of a screen is mentioned in the annotations of that same screen. Check this again yourself, and assess whether a screen really shows the behavior or only cites the code.

# Attached documents

One zip file `metis-review-pack-addendum-onboarding.zip`, whose folder `metis-review-pack-addendum-onboarding/` holds:

1. `Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_Addendum_Onboarding_v1.0.md`: the BRD addendum, the main source. The images in the file point to `../wireframes/png/`, which are exactly the files in `png/` of the zip.
2. `Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.3.md`: the main BRD.
3. `design/2026-10-02-onboarding-design.md` and `design/option-catalogue.md`: the design spec and the option catalogue.
4. `research/research-competitors.md`, `research/research-onboarding-patterns.md`, `research/research-ai-onboarding.md`: market research notes.
5. `wireframes-digest.md` and `manifest.json`: the text and annotations of every wireframe; the mapping from screens to requirement codes.
6. `png/`: the 12 new wireframes (46 to 57) and the 6 original screens (04, 07, 08, 11, 14, 36).

# How to read the documents

1. Unzip the zip with the code execution tool. List every file with its size. If you cannot open the zip, stop and tell me.
2. Read the whole BRD addendum, skipping no section.
3. Read the relevant sections of BRD 4.3: 4.5, 5.2, 7.1, 7.9, the modules M02, M03, M04, M05, the requirements CHR-17, CHG-06, CHG-10, and Sections 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19.
4. Read the design spec and the option catalogue to understand the reason for each choice.
5. Look at all 12 new wireframe images and the 6 original images; use `wireframes-digest.md` to read the small text exactly. If you cannot view the images, say so clearly at the top of the report and tag the layout comments with [Limited visual assessment].
6. Verify the market claims in Appendix D against the research notes; if you can reach the web, re-check the important URLs.
7. Then carry out parts A to H.

# Task

## A. Is the 30-minute goal feasible

- Go through the journey step by step (Sections 6.1 and 6.5): the realistic time for a mid-sized company (state the assumptions), bottlenecks, the risk of going over 30 minutes.
- Whether the definition of "aha" is right for a C-level leader; propose a change if needed.
- Compared with the market (monday magic, Jira Rovo, Microsoft Planner, ServiceNow SPM, Smartsheet): where Metis is better and where it is worse.

## B. Quality of the requirements

- The 40 ONB requirements: which acceptance criteria cannot be tested; ambiguities; missing requirements; overlaps.
- Whether the split into 27 P0 and 13 P1 is reasonable in terms of value and risk (without considering team size).
- The 8 rules BR-43 to BR-50 and the 20 changes in Section 13: whether they contradict BRD 4.3; cross-check every "Today in v4.3" column.

## C. The experience for C-level leaders

- The pre-filled part and the three framing questions (Sections 6.2, 6.3): whether they follow the spirit of "ask outside-in" and contain no numbers; which question should be replaced and with what.
- The question cards, the limit of 10 cards, asking while reading, Portfolio X-ray, the dry run of the approval flow, the launch page, delegation: friction points, the risk of giving up, proposals.
- Nielsen's ten heuristic principles for the 12 screens: location (file name), principle, severity 0 to 4, proposal.

## D. AI architecture, MCP and security

- Using the Draft workspace as the draft (Section 9.2) in place of a separate staging layer: right or wrong, risks, conditions.
- The setup tool group (Section 7.1), the onboarding token, one pipeline for two drivers (Sections 9.5 and 12).
- The guardrails (Section 11) checked against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications 2025: the remaining vulnerabilities; concrete attack scenarios such as indirect prompt injection through documents, probing for the data of other customers, abusing tools, running up costs; proposed controls.
- Data and legal: customer consent, data masking, sub-processors, Article 50 of the EU AI Act, file retention. Tag [Needs verification] on every legal point you are not sure about.

## E. Adopting in-flight projects (Section 9.3)

- Recording "completed before Metis" without creating an approval decision, and taking the commitment baseline from the imported data: whether this is sound for governance and audit; risks; proposals.

## F. Wireframes 46 to 57

- Coverage: from `manifest.json`, confirm that every P0 requirement of ONB has a screen; list the requirements that are only cited by code but that the screen does not show.
- For each screen: whether its purpose is clear (1 to 5), the main problem, the proposed fix.
- Consistency of the sample data (Nova Energy, Kite Logistics) across the 12 screens, and with the original screens 04, 07, 08, 11, 14, 36.
- Accessibility: states that have a shape and a word, keyboard operation, phone screens.

## G. Market evidence

- Check Appendix D line by line: whether the source really says what is claimed; which lines need the tag [Needs verification]; whether any important evidence has been left out.

## H. Refinement requests and questions for the client

- A table with the columns: Code (OB-01, OB-02…), Target (section, requirement code or file name), Problem, Evidence, Specific proposed fix, Priority (Must, Should, Could), Effort (S, M, L). Divide it into three groups: BRD addendum, Wireframes, Architecture and security. Sort by priority.
- Questions for the client that are not yet in D-01 to D-39 and Q-01 to Q-18.

# Rules

- Respect the product owner's decisions in the Context part. If you think a decision is wrong, say so plainly with evidence and consequences, but do not propose cutting scope because of team size.
- Every finding points to evidence: a section or code in the BRD addendum (for example ONB-15, BR-47, D-32), a code in BRD 4.3, or a wireframe file name (for example 48-onboarding-draft-cockpit).
- Separate clearly "Observation from the documents" and "Industry knowledge". Tag [Needs verification] on market, price and legal information that you are not certain about.
- Do not invent figures. When estimating, state the assumptions and use ranges.
- The data in the wireframes is fictional sample data, and the wireframes are at mid-fidelity: do not grade the final aesthetics.
- Write in Vietnamese, in short active sentences; keep English terms and codes unchanged.

# Output

A single Markdown file named `metis-review-addendum-onboarding.md`, created as a downloadable file. If you cannot create a file, print the whole content in one markdown block. Structure:

1. Executive summary: the conclusion on merging into the main BRD (Go, Go with conditions, Not yet); 5 things to do right away; the 5 biggest risks.
2. Parts A to G in order.
3. The refinement table and the questions for the client (part H).
4. Appendix: the files read, the assumptions, the list of [Needs verification] points.

If the content is too long for one answer, create the file part by part and then join the parts; do not shorten the table in part H.
